transport: real-streamable-http for public inventory/resources/refusals; test-only local filesystem channel for internal recovery

runtime_injections.scope: owned disposable child processes only; two fixture actor IDs; no runtime endpoint or packaged helper
runtime_injections.justification: F4 retires public recovery tools. The local test channel calls the installed Core admission facade and durable control plane while retaining real preparation, confirmation, CAS, workers, journals and restart behavior. Actor IDs preserve audit assertions but this channel is not an authentication or permission test. Public MCP inventory/resources and refusal of removed DLQ calls still use real HTTP. Manual DLQ replay assertions are superseded by refusal and exact preservation of the terminal row; no removed workflow is reintroduced.
Expose the committed queued control-plane state long enough to exercise internal-control queued replay and cancellation without racing the owned preparation consumer.
Advance the confirmation-token clock by 600 seconds to exercise the internal expired-token start refusal without a five-minute wall-clock sleep.

Hold the already-durable first preparing phase behind a bounded cross-process release file until the second internal fixture actor observes and replays it; after release the unmodified real 1500-board preparation proceeds. The wrapper prints a chained traceback only when that production operation unexpectedly fails.

runtime_injections.scope: first recovery dispatch in the controlled-clock lifecycle only
runtime_injections.justification: Raise the declared test-only installed_e2e_dispatch_response_lost exception once after the real dispatcher durably enqueues recovery work, then prove an identical internal start retry rediscovers the committed attempt without creating another run. The local channel preserves this explicit injected code; it does not emulate the retired MCP error mapping or reclassify unexpected runtime failures.

runtime_injections.scope: building-gate server lifecycle only (hard-kill adoption test)
runtime_injections.justification: After production's REAL atomic Grafx active_generation.json pointer switch has returned durable, record its path in a signal file and block the native worker thread so the test can hard-kill its owned child tree (taskkill /PID /T /F on Windows includes the venv launcher descendants). The harness observes for 660s, covering the unchanged 600s productive attempt budget plus bounded margin. The hook also recognizes the historical phase=building shape, but the current assertion requires the Grafx pointer. Nothing is skipped or mocked; the write itself is the unmodified production write.

runtime_injections.scope: controlled-clock-fence-loss server lifecycle only; exact run_id+epoch target file; one-shot
runtime_injections.justification: Deterministic REAL writer-fence loss: the acquire wrapper records the productive lease unchanged. After the real atomic Grafx active-generation switch, that lease is released once through its official path (no artificial exception, SQL or fabricated terminal). The pointer contains no run/epoch, so correlation is limited to the sole targeted recovery run in this isolated process. The next productive fence check must reject; the worker persists the terminal outcome. The test preserves the switched pointer bytes as evidence.

runtime_injections.scope: resume-gate restart lifecycle only; exact run_id+epoch target file, one-shot
runtime_injections.justification: Cooperative hold of the REAL native operation for the exact resumed run/epoch N+1 written by the test BEFORE the restart server exists, so the canonical internal resume replay (same actor, same reason, strictly before terminal) can be proven to preserve the exact persisted N+1 identity and exactly one recovery dispatch with zero epoch N+2, while its documented live projection (state/phase/reason_code/progress_seq/heartbeat_at/updated_at/active_elapsed_ms) legitimately advances under the native gate — total payload identity is NOT claimed. Claim/heartbeat stay fully productive during the hold; the release file is written unconditionally in the test's finally, and a 120s deadline proceeds WITHOUT fabricating any error while leaving a timeout marker the test must prove absent.

runtime_injections.scope: z2-tamper server lifecycle only; exact run_id+epoch+variant target file written by the test after prepare+confirm and before the internal start; one-shot
runtime_injections.justification: Production creates the durable worker-inputs artifact INSIDE prepare_durable_start, so no confirm-to-start tamper window exists. The wrapper calls the REAL put first; for the exact targeted run/epoch it then locates the hash-keyed artifact (worker_inputs_<SHA256(run_id)>__attempt-N), records a signal with run/epoch/variant/path/original SHA256, and unlinks it (missing) or truncates it to invalid JSON (corrupt) strictly before the put returns — therefore strictly before the recovery dispatch exists. A test-only tripwire on GlobalDiscoveryWriterLease.acquire writes a marker and fails if the targeted run's owner ever reaches the writer lane; the test must prove the marker ABSENT. The correct zero-work claim is: zero writer lease, zero reconcile/cutover, zero physical mutation of the observed global tree — the input READ itself legitimately happens inside the native wrapper, which fails typed.

runtime_injections.scope: adoption-restart server lifecycle only (hard-kill restart); single signal
runtime_injections.justification: Writes ONE UTC timestamp at the restarted recovery poller's first entry and then delegates to the REAL _poll unchanged. The bounded-takeover proof anchors on persisted ground truth: adopted claimed_at must be >= the old claim expiry and <= max(old claim expiry, this first-poll signal) + poll interval + fixed margin — never on a wall-clock observation that includes installed boot/readiness time.

runtime_injections.scope: adoption-restart server lifecycle only (hard-kill restart); exact run_id+epoch target file, one-shot
runtime_injections.justification: Cooperative hold positioned AFTER the adopting claim transaction (which carries the A5R2 exactly-once crash charge) has durably COMMITTED and BEFORE _run_attempt starts any physical operation. At the gate the test proves the EXACT settled accounting from the SQL ground truth: active == pre_active + gap and cumulative == pre_cumulative + gap with gap = min(old claim expiry, active deadline) - pre heartbeat, plus heartbeat_at/updated_at rebased to the adopting claim's own claimed_at — before releasing any new work. The release file is written unconditionally in the test's finally; a 120s deadline proceeds WITHOUT fabricating any error while leaving a timeout marker the test must prove absent. The wrapper delegates to the REAL _submit_claim unchanged.

No scheduler code, clock, handler, or source-revision fence is patched; the explicit authoritative-board mutation scenarios continue to prove real snapshot-drift refusal.

fixture_mutations.surface: Stopped-server filesystem relocation of the observed KG storage tree
fixture_mutations.justification: Fresh okto-pulse init first proves Global Discovery bootstrap. Then, while the owned server is stopped and CLI handles are closed, the complete global storage directory is relocated to a backup inside the disposable root and recreated empty. This removes the active-generation pointer and all physical generation contents together, simulating confirmed total loss. Admission logic, wait semantics, census size and ports remain unchanged.
Advance the production relational source-revision trigger to prove internal confirm/start fail closed on a stale snapshot fingerprint.

Create one terminal delivery, then prove all retired public DLQ calls are refused over real HTTP and preserve the exact row. Test teardown removes only this unchanged synthetic row under a write transaction; identity collisions or any row mutation fail instead of overwriting/deleting evidence. Later installed cases retain the same runtime but do not inherit this injected DLQ. No manual DLQ replay workflow remains.

fixture_mutations.surface: Stopped-server filesystem relocation of the observed KG storage tree
fixture_mutations.justification: The Z2 and hard-kill tests each need a fresh legitimate recovery admission after an earlier successful recovery, so the SAME declared total-loss relocation is reapplied per test with the server stopped: the complete data_dir/global tree moves to a unique backup inside the isolated root and is recreated empty (CONFIRMED_ABSENT). Nothing is deleted.
